title: Making of the Constitution
desc: Constituent Assembly: formation, composition, committees, enactment and enforcement of the Constitution

basic.q: Who first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India, in 1934?
basic.e: M.N. Roy, a pioneer of the communist movement in India, first proposed the idea of a Constituent Assembly in 1934.

basic.q: In which year did the Indian National Congress officially demand a Constituent Assembly to frame India's Constitution?
basic.e: In 1935, the INC officially demanded a Constituent Assembly for the first time, a year after M.N. Roy first raised the idea.

basic.q: The British Government first accepted the demand for a Constituent Assembly 'in principle' through which of the following?
basic.e: The August Offer of 1940 was where the British Government first accepted, in principle, the demand for a Constituent Assembly.

basic.q: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan's scheme, what was the originally envisaged total strength of the Constituent Assembly?
basic.e: The Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) envisaged a total strength of 389 — 296 from British India and 93 from the princely states.

basic.q: On what date did the Constituent Assembly hold its first meeting?
basic.e: The Constituent Assembly held its first meeting on December 9, 1946; it was boycotted by the Muslim League and attended by only 207 members.

basic.q: Who was elected as the temporary (provisional) Chairman of the Constituent Assembly at its first sitting, following French practice?
basic.e: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member present, was elected temporary Chairman, following the French practice of the eldest member presiding initially.

basic.q: Who was elected the permanent Chairman (President) of the Constituent Assembly on December 11, 1946?
basic.e: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected the permanent Chairman/President of the Constituent Assembly on December 11, 1946.

basic.q: Who moved the historic 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly on December 13, 1946?
basic.e: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution, which laid down the fundamentals and philosophy of the constitutional structure and later shaped the Preamble.

basic.q: When was the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly constituted?
basic.e: The Drafting Committee was set up on August 29, 1947, with the task of preparing the draft Constitution.

basic.q: Who served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee?
basic.e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the seven-member Drafting Committee and is recognised as the 'Father of the Constitution of India'.

basic.q: Following the Indian Independence Act of 1947, the total strength of the Constituent Assembly was reduced from 389 to how many?
basic.e: After the Muslim League members from Pakistan-bound areas withdrew, the Assembly's strength fell from 389 to 299 (229 from provinces, 70 from princely states).

basic.q: On which date did the Constituent Assembly formally adopt the Constitution of India?
basic.e: The Constitution was declared as passed and adopted on November 26, 1949, now celebrated as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas).

basic.q: On which date did most provisions of the Constitution of India come into force?
basic.e: The remaining (major) part of the Constitution came into force on January 26, 1950, the 'date of its commencement', celebrated as Republic Day.

basic.q: January 26 was chosen as the Constitution's date of commencement mainly because it was the anniversary of which earlier event?
o: The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly
Purna Swaraj Day, declared by the INC's Lahore Session
The passing of the Objectives Resolution
The Cabinet Mission's arrival in India
basic.e: January 26 commemorates Purna Swaraj Day, celebrated in 1930 following the Lahore Session (December 1929) resolution of the INC.

basic.q: The Constitution as adopted on November 26, 1949 originally contained a Preamble, how many Articles, and how many Schedules?
basic.e: As adopted, the Constitution contained a Preamble, 395 Articles and 8 Schedules (the numbers have since grown through amendments).

basic.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act inserted Article 394-A, providing for an authoritative Hindi text of the Constitution?
basic.e: The 58th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1987 inserted Article 394-A, providing for an authoritative Hindi translation of the Constitution.

basic.q: Who was appointed as the Constitutional Advisor (Legal Advisor) to the Constituent Assembly?
basic.e: Sir B.N. Rau served as the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly, preparing the initial framework used by the Drafting Committee.

basic.q: Who calligraphed the original Constitution of India in a flowing italic style?
basic.e: Prem Behari Narain Raizada hand-wrote (calligraphed) the original English text of the Constitution in a flowing italic style.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. M.N. Roy first proposed the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934.
2. The Indian National Congress officially demanded a Constituent Assembly in that same year, 1934.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the INC officially demanded a Constituent Assembly only in 1935, a year after Roy's proposal.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Cripps Proposals of 1942:
1. They were accepted by the Muslim League.
2. The Muslim League wanted India divided into two autonomous states with two separate Constituent Assemblies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect — the Cripps Proposals were rejected by the Muslim League.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Cabinet Mission Plan's scheme for the Constituent Assembly:
1. Of the 389 total seats, 296 were allotted to British India and 93 to the princely states.
2. Seats allotted to British Indian provinces were divided among Muslims, Sikhs and General communities in proportion to population.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct features of the Cabinet Mission Plan's scheme for constituting the Assembly.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Elections to the Constituent Assembly in July-August 1946 were held for the 93 seats allotted to the princely states.
2. The princely states' seats remained unfilled as they initially decided to stay away from the Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect — elections were held only for the 296 seats allotted to British Indian provinces; princely-state representatives were to be nominated, not elected, and those seats stayed vacant initially.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly:
1. It was held on December 9, 1946.
2. It was attended by all 389 members originally envisaged.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the meeting was attended by only 207 members, as the Muslim League boycotted it.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Objectives Resolution:
1. It was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946.
2. It was unanimously adopted by the Assembly on January 22, 1947.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct. The Objectives Resolution, moved by Nehru, was unanimously adopted and later shaped the Preamble.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the changes made by the Indian Independence Act, 1947 to the Constituent Assembly:
1. It made the Assembly a fully sovereign body, empowered to frame any Constitution it pleased.
2. It also made the Assembly a legislative body, performing constitutional and ordinary lawmaking functions on separate days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct features introduced by the Indian Independence Act, 1947.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. After the Muslim League's withdrawal, the Assembly's strength was reduced from 389 to 299.
2. The princely states' representation fell from 93 to 70 as part of this reduction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — the strength fell to 299 overall, with provinces' representation falling to 229 and princely states' to 70.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about committees of the Constituent Assembly:
1. The Union Constitution Committee was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.
2. The Provincial Constitution Committee was chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the Provincial Constitution Committee was chaired by Sardar Patel; Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the original seven-member Drafting Committee:
1. It was chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
2. B.L. Mitter, who resigned due to ill health, was replaced by T.T. Krishnamachari.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — B.L. Mitter was replaced by N. Madhava Rau; T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan, who died in 1948.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the enactment of the Constitution:
1. The final draft was introduced in the Assembly for its first reading on November 4, 1948.
2. The Constitution was declared passed after its third reading on November 26, 1949.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct, describing the sequence of the Constitution's first and third readings.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the enforcement of the Constitution:
1. Provisions relating to citizenship and elections came into force on November 26, 1949 itself.
2. The remaining provisions came into force on January 26, 1950, referred to as the date of commencement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct descriptions of the Constitution's staggered enforcement.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about functions performed by the Constituent Assembly besides constitution-making:
1. It adopted the national flag on July 22, 1947.
2. It adopted the national anthem and national song on January 24, 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — the Assembly performed several functions beyond drafting the Constitution, including adopting the flag, anthem, and song.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Hindi text of the Constitution:
1. The Constitution, as originally enacted in 1949, provided for an authoritative Hindi text.
2. Article 394-A, inserted by the 58th Amendment Act of 1987, now deems the published Hindi translation authoritative.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect — the original Constitution made no provision for an authoritative Hindi text; this was added only later.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Experts Committee appointed by the Congress party:
1. It was appointed on July 8, 1946, while elections to the Constituent Assembly were still in progress.
2. It was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct features of the Congress party's Experts Committee of 1946.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements regarding criticism of the Constituent Assembly:
1. Critics argued it was not a representative body since members were not directly elected on universal adult franchise.
2. Winston Churchill remarked that the Assembly represented 'only one major community in India'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — these are among the common criticisms levelled against the Constituent Assembly.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about important facts related to the Constitution's making:
1. Prem Behari Narain Raizada calligraphed the original Constitution in a flowing italic style.
2. Beohar Rammanohar Sinha illuminated and ornamented the original Preamble.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — these artists, associated with Shantiniketan, were responsible for the Constitution's calligraphy and artwork.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements comparing constitution-making timelines:
1. India's Constituent Assembly took about 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to complete its work.
2. This was longer than the time taken by the framers of the American Constitution but shorter than that taken by Australia's framers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — the U.S. took under 4 months, Australia about 9 years, placing India's roughly 3 years in between.

advanced.q:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. August Offer
2. Cripps Proposals
3. Cabinet Mission's arrival in India
4. M.N. Roy's proposal for a Constituent Assembly
advanced.e: Correct order: M.N. Roy's proposal (1934) → August Offer (1940) → Cripps Proposals (1942) → Cabinet Mission (1946).

advanced.q: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Drafting Committee?
o: It was chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
It sat for only 141 days, taking less than six months to prepare its draft
It prepared only a single, final draft of the Constitution, published in February 1948
advanced.e: The Drafting Committee actually prepared two drafts — the first in February 1948 and a revised second draft in October 1948 after considering public comments. The other statements are correct.

advanced.q: N. Madhava Rau joined the Drafting Committee as a replacement for which original member, who resigned due to ill health?
advanced.e: B.L. Mitter resigned from the Drafting Committee due to ill health and was replaced by N. Madhava Rau.

advanced.q: T.T. Krishnamachari joined the Drafting Committee as a replacement for which original member, who died in 1948?
advanced.e: D.P. Khaitan died in 1948, and T.T. Krishnamachari was inducted into the Drafting Committee in his place.

advanced.q: Of the total 299 members of the Constituent Assembly on the day the Constitution was adopted, how many were actually present and signed it?
advanced.e: Only 284 of the 299 members were present on November 26, 1949 and appended their signatures to the Constitution.

advanced.q: Which of the following is NOT correct about the enforcement of the Constitution?
o: Certain provisions relating to citizenship and elections came into force on November 26, 1949
Most provisions came into force on January 26, 1950
The Government of India Act, 1935 and the Indian Independence Act, 1947 were repealed on the Constitution's commencement
The Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949 was also repealed along with the other two Acts on commencement
advanced.e: The Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949 was specifically continued, not repealed, when the Constitution commenced. The other statements are correct.

advanced.q: Which of the following was NOT a member of the original seven-member Drafting Committee as constituted on August 29, 1947?
advanced.e: T.T. Krishnamachari joined the Drafting Committee only later, replacing D.P. Khaitan after his death in 1948 — he was not part of the original seven.

advanced.q: The 'Objectives Resolution' moved by Nehru in December 1946 most directly and eventually shaped which part of the final Constitution?
o: The Directive Principles of State Policy
advanced.e: A modified version of the Objectives Resolution forms the Preamble of the present Constitution.

advanced.q: As per the chapter's comparison of constitution-framing timelines, which country's constitution-makers took the shortest time to complete their work?
advanced.e: The framers of the U.S.A.'s Constitution took less than 4 months (May-September 1787), the shortest among the countries compared.

advanced.q: How many sessions did the Constituent Assembly hold in total while making the Constitution?
advanced.e: The Constituent Assembly held 11 sessions over a period of 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.

advanced.q: While drafting the Constitution, the Constitution-makers are said to have gone through the constitutions of approximately how many countries?
advanced.e: The Constitution-makers examined the constitutions of about 60 countries before finalising India's Constitution.

advanced.q: The total expenditure incurred on making the Constitution of India is stated to be approximately:
advanced.e: The total expenditure on making the Constitution amounted to approximately ₹64 lakh.

advanced.q: When the Constituent Assembly met as a legislative body (Dominion Legislature) rather than as a constitution-making body, who chaired its proceedings?
advanced.e: As a legislative body, the Assembly was chaired by G.V. Mavalankar; as a constituent body, it was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad.

advanced.q: Which sub-committee of the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas was chaired by J.B. Kripalani?
o: Excluded and Partially Excluded Areas Sub-Committee
advanced.e: J.B. Kripalani chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee, one of five sub-committees under Sardar Patel's Advisory Committee.

advanced.q: Which of the following correctly identifies who prepared material and drafted a resolution 'closely resembling the Objectives Resolution', even before the Constituent Assembly itself convened?
advanced.e: The Congress's Experts Committee, appointed in July 1946 while elections were still underway, drafted a resolution closely resembling the later Objectives Resolution.

advanced.q: Which of the following is correctly identified as the role played by S.N. Mukherjee in the making of the Constitution?
o: Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly
advanced.e: S.N. Mukherjee served as the chief draftsman of the Constitution within the Constituent Assembly Secretariat.

advanced.q: Which of the following symbols was adopted as the official seal of the Constituent Assembly?
advanced.e: The elephant was adopted as the symbol (seal) of the Constituent Assembly.

advanced.q: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding comparisons of constitution-framing time?
o: The U.S.A.'s framers took less than 4 months
India's Constituent Assembly took less time than Canada's framers
Naziruddin Ahmed sarcastically called the Drafting Committee a 'Drifting Committee'
advanced.e: Canada's framers took about 2 years and 6 months, which is actually less than India's roughly 2 years and 11 months — so India did not take less time than Canada. The other statements are correct.

upsc.q:
Match List-I (Committee of the Constituent Assembly) with List-II (its Chairman) and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I:
A. Union Powers Committee
B. Provincial Constitution Committee
C. Drafting Committee
D. Rules of Procedure Committee
List-II:
1. Jawaharlal Nehru
2. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
3. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
4. Dr. Rajendra Prasad
upsc.e: Union Powers Committee — Nehru; Provincial Constitution Committee — Patel; Drafting Committee — Ambedkar; Rules of Procedure Committee — Rajendra Prasad.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): The Constituent Assembly is criticised by some as not having been a 'sovereign body' at its inception.
Reason (R): It was constituted on the basis of proposals made by the British Government, and its early sessions were held with that Government's permission.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: Both are true, and R correctly explains why critics viewed the Assembly, at its inception, as lacking full sovereignty — since it originated from and initially operated under British sanction.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about the leadership of the Constituent Assembly:
1. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was elected temporary Chairman as the oldest member present, following French practice.
2. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent Chairman on December 11, 1946.
3. H.C. Mukherjee remained the Assembly's sole Vice-President throughout its existence.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — the Assembly later resolved to have two Vice-Presidents, and V.T. Krishnamachari was elected as the second on July 16, 1947.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): The strength of the Constituent Assembly fell from 389 to 299 after the Indian Independence Act, 1947.
Reason (R): Muslim League members hailing from areas included in Pakistan withdrew from the Constituent Assembly for India.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: Both are true, and the Muslim League's withdrawal directly explains the fall in strength from 389 to 299.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about the enactment of the Constitution:
1. As many as 7,653 amendments were proposed during the second reading, of which 2,473 were actually discussed.
2. The Constitution as adopted on November 26, 1949 contained a Preamble, 395 Articles and 8 Schedules.
3. The third reading of the draft Constitution began on November 14, 1949.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements accurately describe stages of the Constitution's enactment process.

upsc.q:
Match List-I (Date) with List-II (Event) and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I:
A. December 9, 1946
B. January 22, 1947
C. November 26, 1949
D. January 26, 1950
List-II:
1. Objectives Resolution adopted
2. First meeting of the Constituent Assembly
3. Constitution adopted by the Assembly
4. Constitution came into full force
upsc.e: Dec 9, 1946 — first meeting; Jan 22, 1947 — Objectives Resolution adopted; Nov 26, 1949 — Constitution adopted; Jan 26, 1950 — full commencement.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): January 26 was chosen as the date of commencement of the Constitution.
Reason (R): It was on this day in 1930 that 'Purna Swaraj Day' was celebrated, following the Lahore Session resolution of the Indian National Congress (December 1929).
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: Both are true, and R correctly explains the historical significance behind choosing January 26 as the Constitution's commencement date.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements regarding criticism of the Constituent Assembly:
1. Critics described it as a 'one-party body in an essentially one-party country', dominated by the Congress.
2. Naziruddin Ahmed sarcastically referred to the Drafting Committee as a 'Drifting Committee' over delays.
3. Lord Viscount Simon and Winston Churchill both praised the Assembly as fully representative of all Indian communities.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — Simon and Churchill actually criticised the Assembly as Hindu-dominated or representing only one community, not praised it.

upsc.q:
Match List-I (Person) with List-II (Role in the making of the Constitution) and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I:
A. Sir B.N. Rau
B. H.V.R. Iyengar
C. S.N. Mukherjee
D. Prem Behari Narain Raizada
List-II:
1. Chief draftsman of the Constitution
2. Constitutional Advisor
3. Calligrapher of the original Constitution
4. Secretary to the Constituent Assembly
upsc.e: B.N. Rau — Constitutional Advisor; H.V.R. Iyengar — Secretary; S.N. Mukherjee — Chief draftsman; Prem Behari Narain Raizada — Calligrapher.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about the Experts Committee appointed by the Congress party in 1946:
1. It was appointed on July 8, 1946, while elections to the Constituent Assembly were still in progress.
2. It was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.
3. Granville Austin credited it with having 'set India on the road to her present Constitution'.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements correctly describe the Congress's Experts Committee and its acknowledged influence on the constitution-making process.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): Critics have argued that lawyer-politician domination of the Constituent Assembly is the main reason for the bulkiness and complicated language of the Constitution.
Reason (R): Other sections of Indian society were, according to critics, not sufficiently represented in the Assembly.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: Both reflect the critics' own reasoning — that lawyer-politician domination, stemming from under-representation of other sections, led to a bulky and legalistic Constitution.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about the Cabinet Mission Plan's seat-allocation scheme:
1. Roughly one seat was allotted for every million of population.
2. Representatives of the princely states were to be elected directly by the people of those states through adult franchise.
3. Representatives of each community in British Indian provinces were elected by members of that community in the provincial legislative assembly, using proportional representation by single transferable vote.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — princely-state representatives were to be nominated by the heads of the princely states, not elected.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): The original Constitution of India, as enacted in 1949, did not contain any authoritative text in the Hindi language.
Reason (R): A provision on this subject was inserted only via Article 394-A, added by the 58th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1987.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: Both statements are factually true, but R describes the later remedy (what was eventually inserted), not the reason why the original 1949 Constitution lacked such a provision — so R does not explain A.

upsc.q:
Match List-I (Reading Stage of the Draft Constitution) with List-II (Date/Description) and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I:
A. First reading
B. Second reading
C. Third reading
D. Final adoption
List-II:
1. November 4, 1948
2. November 15, 1948 to October 17, 1949
3. Began November 14, 1949
4. November 26, 1949
upsc.e: First reading — Nov 4, 1948; Second reading — Nov 15, 1948 to Oct 17, 1949; Third reading — began Nov 14, 1949; Final adoption — Nov 26, 1949.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): After the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the Constituent Assembly performed both constituent and legislative functions.
Reason (R): It met as the Dominion Legislature (chaired by G.V. Mavalankar) and as the constitution-making body (chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad) on separate days.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: Both are true, and R correctly explains how the Assembly's dual constituent-cum-legislative role was structured, with different chairs for each function.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about the enforcement of the Constitution:
1. Provisions on citizenship and elections came into force on November 26, 1949.
2. Most other provisions came into force on January 26, 1950.
3. The Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949 was also repealed on the Constitution's commencement, along with the Government of India Act, 1935.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — the Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949 was continued, not repealed, unlike the Government of India Act, 1935 and the Indian Independence Act, 1947.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): The Constituent Assembly has been criticised by some as not being a fully 'representative body'.
Reason (R): Its members were elected indirectly, by members of the provincial legislative assemblies, who themselves had been elected on a limited (not universal adult) franchise.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: Both are true, and R correctly explains the basis of this criticism — the Assembly's indirect, limited-franchise election process.

upsc.q:
Match List-I (Committee) with List-II (Chairman) and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I:
A. Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas
B. States Committee (Committee for Negotiating with States)
C. Steering Committee
D. Credentials Committee
List-II:
1. Jawaharlal Nehru
2. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
3. Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar
4. Dr. Rajendra Prasad
upsc.e: Advisory Committee on FR/Minorities — Patel; States Committee — Nehru; Steering Committee — Rajendra Prasad; Credentials Committee — Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): The Drafting Committee is regarded as the most important of all the committees of the Constituent Assembly.
Reason (R): It was specifically entrusted with preparing the actual draft of the new Constitution, incorporating the proposals of the various other committees.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: Both are true, and R correctly explains why the Drafting Committee held such central importance among all the Assembly's committees.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about facts related to the making of the Constitution:
1. The elephant was adopted as the symbol (seal) of the Constituent Assembly.
2. Sir B.N. Rau, besides being Constitutional Advisor, was also a formal member of the seven-member Drafting Committee.
3. Nand Lal Bose and Beohar Rammanohar Sinha, artists from Shantiniketan, beautified the original Constitution.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — Sir B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor, but was not himself one of the seven formal members of the Drafting Committee.
